title: Origin and proxy credentials in one request
summary: One synthetic request carrying a different Basic token in each of the Authorization and Proxy-Authorization headers.
rationale: The two headers address different recipients: the proxy consumes its credentials and the origin server its own. Both values are credentials in the same input, so each needs its own exact span; merging them or reporting only one leaves a credential exposed.

expectation.rationale: Flag both tokens, each with its own extent. RFC 9110 gives Proxy-Authorization to the first inbound proxy that demanded it and passes Authorization to the origin server unmodified.

sources.supports: the Proxy-Authorization header field applies only to the next inbound proxy that demanded authentication
A proxy forwarding a request MUST NOT modify any Authorization header fields in that request

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
